proposals.reason: Company-specific and still escalating: board probe of the CEO (11-08), DOJ criminal inquiry into Megaspeed (11-09), a House reply due 11-11; worst day against the index since January 2025 on 3.9x volume while every other chip stock rallied.

reasoning.what_changed: -4.3% to 178.67 on 3.9x volume on a day SPY rose 2.4% and the chip index 6.9%; down as much as 8.8% intraday; below the 20-day low; -21% in 20 days.
reasoning.story: 11-08: the board opened an independent investigation after NYT/FT reports that US intelligence believes a Megaspeed executive passed information to Beijing and targeted Jensen Huang, who admitted an affair in a staff memo and remains CEO. 11-09: NYT says the Commerce probe of Megaspeed chip diversion moved to the Justice Department as a criminal inquiry; Trump said the FBI is looking into Huang over 'something else'; a shareholder class action is reported. No rating change found; Bernstein and RBC reiterated Outperform. The first NYT report was about 10-29, so this is an escalation of a story that has already cost about 20%.
reasoning.chart: For: a break of the 20-day low on the heaviest relative volume in the screen, with buyers plainly preferring AMD (+13%) and Broadcom (+8.8%). Against: RSI 27, 3.6 ATR below the 20-day mean, 8% above the 52-week low at 163.90, and more than half of the intraday fall was bought back by the close.
reasoning.coming: CPI Tuesday 8:30 AM ET; CoreWeave Tuesday after the close; the House briefing reply Wednesday 11-11; AMAT and Cisco Thursday after the close. NVDA reports 11-17 after the close: the 4-session limit exits Friday 11-13, clear of it.
reasoning.case_against: An oversold stock with two-way headline risk: one clearing statement from the board or the Justice Department reverses it, and the news is ten days old. The setup's history (relative weakness short, 3 days, against SPY) is +66 bp and 59% winners, but NVDA's own 11 events average +33 bp with one at -1,769 bp. The challenge found no wrong fact and no reversal, but showed that SMH, the screen's hedge, buys back part of the short (NVDA is a top holding, beta 0.69) the day after a 6.9% chip rally; the hedge is changed to QQQ for that reason. It didn't win because the investigation widened on both days since the weekend and the stock closed at its relative low on the news.

proposals.wrong_if: The board's independent directors, the Justice Department or the FBI say Huang is not a subject or the probe found nothing; or the 11-11 House reply closes the matter; or the White House confirms Huang on the Shenzhen trip. Any of these inside the window means the overhang is lifting.
proposals.hedge_why: Correlation 0.65, beta 1.12, so equal dollars are close to market-neutral. SMH (0.75, beta 0.69) is tighter but NVDA is one of its largest holdings and equal dollars would leave the pair net long chips after a 6.9% day. QQQ leaves some chips-against-tech exposure, which is short the group that just bounced.
